messages:
sam: Quick sync — product wants per-customer SLOs surfaced in Console + a tenant-level noisy-neighbor dashboard. Need runtime/infra inputs on what we can safely emit and how to keep cardinality down. Who can weigh in on metrics + routing metadata?

devon: Are we talking raw per-request labels or pre-aggregated counters? Core ask is: show a per-org view of cost, latency, and 'noisy neighbor' signals (queue backlog, GPU steal).

alexa: For the dashboard UX we'd want p50/p95/p99 latency by org, token/sec (ingest vs generation), and a cache prefix hit-rate. Also useful: 'route policy applied' per sampled request so support can see when fallback routing happened.

maria: From runtime: we can emit org-scoped metrics but need to be careful. Attaching high-cardinality labels (full org_id + model_revision + route) to every metric will explode TSDB cost. Suggest two-tier approach: low-cardinality continuous metrics + sampled detailed traces.

tufan: Proposal: emit these continuous series at per-org rollup granularity (1m):
```
metric: redwood.runtime.org_rollup.requests_total
labels: [org_tenant, region]
aggregation: sum
retention: 30d

metric: redwood.runtime.org_rollup.token_seconds
labels: [org_tenant]
aggregation: sum,p90,p99
retention: 14d
```
Detailed route_decision and model_variant tags -> emit only for 1% deterministic sample (org hash). That gives us traceability without cardinality blowup.

devon: OK re: ACLs and isolation — dashboards must enforce backend scoping so customers only see their org metrics. Who owns the enforcement? Platform or Console?

alexa: Platform should provide a filtered metrics API (query params: org_id, time_range) and Console calls that API. Platform must return 403 for cross-org queries.

maria: We can add `org_id` scoping into the metrics API. Implementation note: if we add org_id as a required query param on rollup endpoints we can avoid adding labels in the TSDB and let the query layer filter by tenant. But we still need per-tenant rollup job that writes per-org series; otherwise querying will be expensive.

tufan: Also need to think about SLO computation: do we compute per-tenant SLOs upstream and store them as metrics, or compute on read? Upstream compute (periodic job) gives faster console UX and predictable cost.

sam: Action items summary: 1) eng-runtime to draft list of minimal rollup metrics + retention (maria) 2) eng-infra to propose storage + rollup job shape (tufan) 3) eng-platform to spec filtered metrics API and ACL checks (devon) 4) devex/console to mock UX and sampling presentation (alexa). Please post small PRs or rough proto snippets in this thread by EOD Wed.

infra-bot: deploy: metrics-rollup-config v2 pushed to staging at 1830456800 — watch for increased TSDB writes. :rocket:

maria: Noted — I'll post the rollup metric list (names/units/retention) in the thread shortly. For visibility: we'll limit detailed tags sample to 0.5% per-org for top-100 orgs, 1% others, configurable.

sam: Thanks all — schedule 30m follow-up Friday to finalize the API contract. If anyone can't make it, drop the proto in here. :+1:
